content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text resolves a challenge by comparing the challenger's covenant-origin chain with Matthew 1:20's own wording rather than by weighing chain against chain by footing.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"never verse by verse: one reading forbids deciding by a single sentence's own words, while the other permits it as part of assessing the link's footing.","why":"The judge cites Matthew 1:20's own sentence as decisive against the challenger's footed analogy, which is a verse-level stating test rather than a chain-by-footing comparison."}
